relevance_reason: The abstract reports CTNS mutations in patients with late-onset cystinosis and in patients with an intermediate phenotype, and relates these mutations to milder disease.

findings.statement: Attard et al. (1999) described late-onset cystinosis as a rarer form of the disorder, characterized by onset of symptoms between 12 and 15 years of age.
quotes: Late-onset cystinosis, a rarer form of the disorder, is characterized by onset of symptoms between 12 and 15 years of age.

findings.statement: Attard et al. (1999) screened the CTNS gene in patients with infantile nephropathic cystinosis, patients with late-onset cystinosis, and patients whose phenotype did not fit the classical definitions. They found 23 different CTNS mutations, 14 of them novel. In 2 patients with late-onset cystinosis, the mutations affected functionally unimportant regions of cystinosin, which the authors concluded accounted for the milder phenotype.
quotes: We found 23 different mutations in CTNS; 14 are novel mutations.
Mutations found in two late-onset patients affect functionally unimportant regions of cystinosin, which accounts for their milder phenotype.

findings.statement: Attard et al. (1999) found that 3 patients had cystinosis onset before 7 years of age but a milder course than the infantile nephropathic form. These patients carried missense mutations in CTNS. The authors suggested that these mutations allow production of functional protein and may mark regions of cystinosin that are not functionally important.
quotes: For three patients, the age of onset of cystinosis was <7 years but the course of the disease was milder than the infantile nephropathic form.
This suggests that the missense mutations found in these individuals allow production of functional protein and may also indicate regions of cystinosin which are not functionally important.

findings.statement: Attard et al. (1999) reported that of 25 patients with infantile nephropathic cystinosis, 12 had 2 severely truncating CTNS mutations, consistent with loss of functional protein. The other 13 had missense mutations or in-frame deletions, predicted to disrupt transmembrane domains and abolish protein function.
quotes: Out of 25 patients with infantile nephropathic cystinosis, 12 have two severely truncating mutations, which is consistent with a loss of functional protein, and 13 have missense or in-frame deletions, which would result in disruption of transmembrane domains and loss of protein function.

relevance_reason: The paper describes six patients with intermediate cystinosis and their CTNS mutations, including two new ones. It also includes functional correction studies.

findings.statement: Thoene et al. (1999) described 6 patients with the intermediate form of cystinosis and identified CTNS mutations, 2 of which had not been reported before. They found that the disease resulted either from compound heterozygosity for one mild mutation and one mutation known to cause nephropathic cystinosis, or from homozygosity for a predicted mild mutation.
quotes: Six patients with the intermediate form of cystinosis are described. Two have new mutations not previously described.
The disease occurs due either to the combination of one mild mutation and one which is known to cause nephropathic cystinosis or to homozygosity for a predicted mild mutation.

findings.statement: Thoene et al. (1999) concluded that intermediate cystinosis results from having at least one mild CTNS mutation: either one mild mutation together with a mutation that causes nephropathic cystinosis, or two copies (homozygosity) of a predicted mild mutation.
quotes: The disease occurs due either to the combination of one mild mutation and one which is known to cause nephropathic cystinosis or to homozygosity for a predicted mild mutation.

findings.statement: Thoene et al. (1999) showed that transfecting cystinotic fibroblasts with normal CTNS cDNA, or with a cDNA carrying a mutation that causes intermediate cystinosis, partially corrected the cells' phenotype.
quotes: Partial phenotypic correction of cystinotic fibroblasts by transfection with normal cDNA or a cDNA derived from a mutation causing intermediate cystinosis is demonstrated.
